text: Right where we left off: a goblin no taller than Jaeha's waist is holding back a boss's sword with one knife. He glances back and asks the obvious question. If Jaeha is in charge, why is he the one bleeding?
Jaeha touches his lip. Blood. That emergency call took far more out of him than a husk ever did.
The goblin spins out from under the blade and kicks the giant sword aside with his bare heel.
Then he grabs Yerin by the collar and Jaeha by the vest and drags them both across the floor like luggage.
A heartbeat later, the sword smashes the spot where they were sitting.
Behind a pillar, a window opens in front of Jaeha. Summon answered: Nib. Far Side scout. Seal one of five. Field form: five minutes.
So the goblin has a name. Nib peers round the pillar and gets straight to business. What is that thing, and what is Jaeha?
Jaeha answers like he's on the job. That's a boss, and he's a trap-tester. He walks in first, so other people don't have to.
Nib doesn't even blink. Then they do the same job. His paid better.
Yerin is still trying to work out why a husk is talking.
There's no time to explain. The knight drags its sword out of the floor and turns toward their pillar.
Nib wants an order. Jaeha has never given one in his life, so he says the only rule he knows. Summons go first?
Nib almost smiles. They always do.
And he's gone, a dark streak across the hall.
From above, you can see how unfair this is: a goblin barely a metre tall, charging a knight four and a half metres high.
His knives rake the back of its knee, and the armour barely scratches.
A window explains why. Nib's seal limits him to twenty percent of his real power.
Twenty percent of himself, and he still runs straight up the knight's sword, muttering that this is embarrassing.
He slashes at the hole where its face should be, but the knight jerks back, and the knife skids off the helm.
Then a huge gauntlet comes round and swats him out of the air.
Nib flies across the hall and craters a pillar. Three minutes thirty-one seconds left.
Jaeha shouts his name before he can stop himself.
Nib lands on his feet in the rubble and spits. The knight is faster than it looks, and its arms are far too long.
Jaeha pulls out his notebook. Slow to turn. Hits whatever is in front of it. And a question mark next to its left shoulder. He needs a closer look. He needs to see what Nib sees.
And the window answers. New skill: Link. See through your summon's eyes and give silent orders, up to fifty metres away. But you will feel its pain too.
Suddenly Jaeha is looking out of Nib's eyes, straight up at the knight.
And Nib's bruised ribs hurt as if they were his own.
But now he can see it. The knight's left shoulder plate is cracked, and it dips when the swing begins.
So Jaeha yells it across the hall. His left shoulder drops before every sweep!
Nib's ear twitches. Stop shouting. He can hear Jaeha thinking now.
So Jaeha thinks instead. The knight winds up. Not yet. Wait for the shoulder.
The plate dips.
Now! Nib drops flat, and the blade passes a finger's width over his back.
Then he springs up inside the knight's guard and rips both knives along the seam under its arm. Violet ash sprays out like blood.
For the first time, the knight staggers. Two minutes fourteen.
Yerin stares at Jaeha. He saw that coming from across the room.
But the knight whirls back faster than ever and drives its pommel down at Nib like a hammer. Nib is still landing. There's nowhere to go.
Another window. New skill: Carry. Take part of your summon's damage into your own body. Overload means bleeding, then collapse.
Jaeha doesn't hesitate. Yes. Give it to him.
The pommel slams down on Nib, and half of the blow simply vanishes into a ring of amber light.
Because across the hall, Jaeha takes it. He folds to his knees, fresh blood running from his nose. Fifty percent of the hit, moved to the Operator.
Yerin doesn't understand. Nothing even touched him.
But Nib understands. And for the first time, the deadpan goblin looks shocked.
He's back at the pillar in a blink, staring down. Jaeha took his hit. Why would he do that?
Jaeha grins through the blood. Because Nib is the one who can actually hurt it.
Nib doesn't answer. The look in his eye says nobody has ever done that for him before.
He turns away and points a knife at Yerin. Strange man. Healer, stop shaking and fix him.
Yerin's hands are shaking. A soft mint light gathers in them anyway. One minute twenty left.
She froze earlier tonight. She is not going to freeze again.
Jaeha notices her hands are still trembling. They can shake and heal at the same time, she tells him.
Jaeha gets back on his feet, notebook open. One more opening like that, and they can end this.
But the knight has gone completely still. Forty seconds left on Nib's clock.
Then it throws back its head and roars, in a language nobody in Seoul has ever heard.
Jaeha and Yerin clamp their hands over their ears. Is that even a language?
Nib doesn't cover his ears. He just stares.
At the badge on the knight's chest: a wall with nine towers.
That's the sigil of the Ninth Wall, he says quietly.
Jaeha has no idea what that means. Does Nib know this knight?
Nib stands at attention, facing the giant that nearly killed them all. That knight was his commander.
